title: Practice prediction: Mile Championship (G1)
sub: Use a real race to try predicting and betting with ¥10,000 of virtual money. We will announce the result after watching the race video together.
how: Read the race conditions and the race card
Look at the odds and the "reasons for popularity"
Build your bets with ¥10,000 of virtual money
Watch the race video, enter the result and check your bets
race: 3-year-olds and up, Open, G1. Weight: 3-year-olds 57kg, 4-year-olds and up 58kg; fillies and mares 2kg less
course: On Kyoto's outer course there is a small hill at the 3rd corner. Horses go up it, then run downhill into the home straight (about 400m). The straight is shorter than Tokyo's (about 526m).
cardNote: Win odds are the final odds just before the start. "Crowd's win chance" = 80 ÷ odds: the chance of winning that the crowd believes, worked back from the odds (using the 80% payout rate). Added together, they come to about 100%.
whyLead: Horses are listed in order of popularity. Read why each horse is (or isn't) popular, and compare it with your own thinking.
reasons: A 3-year-old gelding from France. Last time he won France's G1 Prix du Moulin de Longchamp, beating three G1 winners in a course-record time. It is his first race in Japan, so how he suits Kyoto is unknown.
A strong mare with three G1 wins (Oka Sho, Shuka Sho, Victoria Mile). Ridden by C. Lemaire. Her first race in about six months, since the Victoria Mile.
Was 2nd in this year's Milers Cup (G2), but since then has finished 8th in the Yasuda Kinen and 11th in the Mainichi Okan.
Won his first G1 in this year's Yasuda Kinen and set a record winning last year's Nakayama Kinen. But he finished 10th in a G1 in France last time, so his popularity dropped.
All three of his wins came at Kyoto, including the Asahi Hai Futurity (G1) at age 2 and this year's Milers Cup (G2). He was 6th in the Fuji Stakes last time. Ridden by Y. Take.
Has won two in a row (Niigata Nippo Sho, Keisei Hai Autumn Handicap G3), but it is unclear whether she can compete with strong G1 rivals: 18th favourite (the least popular).
A 6-year-old mare who won the Queen Stakes (G3) last time. She was 5th in this year's Victoria Mile (G1).
Winner of this year's NHK Mile Cup (G1) and has never finished worse than 2nd in five starts. Last time, in his first race at 2000m and against older horses, he was 2nd. Ridden by J. Moreira.
Won this year's Kyoto Kinen (G2), but recently finished 8th in the Takarazuka Kinen and 7th in the All Comers over longer distances. This time the distance is 600m shorter.
Was 3rd in the Mile Championship two years ago and won the Tokyo Shimbun Hai (G3), but this year he has struggled: 13th in the Yasuda Kinen and 7th in the Fuji Stakes.
2nd in last year's Mile Championship and 2nd in this year's Yasuda Kinen (a neck behind the winner). Now 7 years old, he returns after about five and a half months off.
Unbeaten in three starts over Kyoto turf 1600m. In good form: 2nd (dead heat) in the Yasuda Kinen and 2nd in the Sprinters Stakes (1200m) last time.
Won this year's New Zealand Trophy (G2) and the Mahoroba Stakes (Open) last time. But in other graded races (10th in the Swan Stakes, etc.) he has not done well.

Has won two G1s at a mile (Hanshin Juvenile Fillies, Oka Sho). She was 4th in the Sprinters Stakes (1200m) last time. As a 3-year-old filly she carries only 55kg, the lightest in the field — the favourite.
2nd in the Keisei Hai Autumn Handicap (G3) last time. It is unclear whether he can compete with strong G1 rivals, so he is not very popular.
2nd in the Swan Stakes (G2, Kyoto 1400m) last time. He has won twice on Kyoto turf. The distance is 200m longer this time.
Won the Sekiya Kinen (G3) by 5 lengths, then was 2nd in the Fuji Stakes (G2), 0.1 seconds behind the winner. Rated for his good form.
3rd in the Swan Stakes (G2) last time. He was 6th in this year's Yasuda Kinen.
hints: Do you believe the "crowd's win chance"? Is any horse rated too high or too low?
Which horses have already won over the same Kyoto turf 1600m?
How might the weight differences (55kg to 58kg) help or hurt?
For horses changing distance (from 1200m, or from 2000m+), can they perform at a mile?
Compared with the Tokyo Sports Hai (G2, 12 runners), how different is the favourite's win chance? Is an 18-runner G1 more likely to produce an upset?
In the paddock video: does the horse look calm and in good condition?
simLead: You have ¥10,000 of virtual money. Choose a bet type and horses, enter an amount (in ¥100 units) and press "Add to slip". You can combine as many bets as you like.
errSame: You chose the same horse (bracket) twice. Please choose different horses.
estNote: Win and place odds are the real final odds. Place odds are announced as a range such as "1.2–1.5", because the payout depends on which other horses also finish in the top 3. Odds for other bet types are estimates calculated from the win odds and differ from the real payouts.
resH: Enter the result (after watching the race video)
resLead: Watch the race video together and listen to the teacher's announcement, then enter the 1st to 3rd horses. For winning tickets, enter the real payout announced (per ¥100) to get an exact result.
errRes: Please choose three different horses for 1st to 3rd.
estWarn: Tickets without an entered payout are calculated with the estimated odds.
reflect: Which popularity rank were your horses? Did you follow the crowd or go against it?
Was your return rate higher or lower than 80% (the payout rate)?
Which viewpoint helped? Which viewpoint do you want to check with data next?
Can one result tell you that a way of betting is right? How many races of data would you need to check it?
src: The race card and odds are based on JRA announcements and news reports. All money is virtual; we do not actually bet (betting is allowed from age 20).
pickHelp: Tap numbers to choose horses (brackets). If you choose several, you buy every combination at once.
